cultureTips.title: The Sacred Greeting: Always Say 'Bonjour'
cultureTips.description: In France, entering any bakery, boutique, taxi, or elevator without an audible 'Bonjour' is considered a serious social blunder. 'Bonjour' is not just a greeting; it is the polite pass-key that acknowledges the other person's humanity.

cultureTips.title: The 'Tu' vs 'Vous' Boundary
cultureTips.description: French draws a strict line between intimacy and respect. Use 'Vous' with shopkeepers, elders, strangers, and professional colleagues. Switch to 'Tu' only when invited ('On peut se tutoyer ?') or among close friends and peers.

cultureTips.title: The Art of 'La Bise' (Cheek Kissing)
cultureTips.description: When greeting friends and family, the French exchange cheek kisses (air kisses making a soft kiss sound while touching cheeks). The count varies by region: 2 kisses in Paris, 3 in Montpellier, and 4 in parts of Normandy.

cultureTips.title: Whisper Volume on Public Transit
cultureTips.description: The Paris Métro and regional trains are shared sanctuaries of calm. Speaking loudly, shouting on phones, or playing music without headphones is deeply frowned upon. Keep voices measured and considerate.

cultureTips.title: Casual Elegance over Gym Wear
cultureTips.description: The French default dress code is smart casual ('BCBG' or relaxed chic). Sweatpants, gym attire, and flip-flops are strictly reserved for the gym, home, or beach, and rarely worn on city streets or in restaurants.

cultureTips.title: The Departure Courtesy: 'Merci, Au Revoir'
cultureTips.description: When leaving any small shop, bakery, or post office, it is customary to call out 'Merci, bonne journée, au revoir !' to the cashier or shopkeeper, maintaining the social circle of respect.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: French Alphabet, Accents & Sounds
lessons.description: Master the French alphabet, essential accents (é, è, ê, ç), and key pronunciation secrets like silent final letters.

questions.prompt: How is the acute accent (l'accent aigu: 'é') pronounced in French?
questions.explanation: The accent aigu ('é') produces a crisp, closed sound like 'ay' in English (e.g. 'café', 'été').

questions.prompt: Match the French accents with their names:
Listen to the word 'Français'. Why does the 'c' have a cedilla (ç)?
options: To make the 'c' sound like a soft 's' before 'a'
To show the word is plural
questions.correctAnswer: To make the 'c' sound like a soft 's' before 'a'
questions.explanation: The cédille ('ç') softens the letter 'C' to an 'S' sound in front of A, O, or U.

questions.prompt: In general, what happens to final consonants (like -d, -s, -t, -x) in French words?
questions.explanation: In French, final consonants like 's' in 'Paris' or 't' in 'chat' are usually silent unless liaison occurs.

questions.prompt: Listen to the pronunciation of 'Paris'. How is it pronounced?
questions.explanation: The final 's' in 'Paris' is silent: pronounced 'Pah-ree'.

questions.sentence: Le mot 'garçon' prend une ___ sous le c.
questions.explanation: 'Garçon' takes a cédille (ç) so it is pronounced 'gar-sohn' instead of 'gar-kohn'.

questions.prompt: Match French vowel combinations with their sounds:
Arrange the words to say: 'The French alphabet'
questions.explanation: 'L'alphabet français' means 'The French alphabet'.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Salutations & Courtesies
lessons.description: Master essential greetings, polite requests, and daily social etiquette in France.

questions.prompt: What is the universal French greeting used throughout the day?
questions.explanation: 'Bonjour' (Good day / Hello) is the fundamental polite greeting in France.

questions.prompt: Match French greetings with their English meanings:
Listen to the phrase. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: 'S'il vous plaît' is the polite form of 'Please'.

questions.sentence: Merci beaucoup ! — De ___ !
questions.explanation: 'De rien' is the most common way to say 'You're welcome' in French.

questions.prompt: Match French courtesies with English:
How do you politely ask 'How are you?' to an adult stranger or professor?
questions.explanation: 'Comment allez-vous ?' uses the formal 'vous' to show respect.

questions.prompt: What does this response express?
questions.explanation: 'Ça va bien, merci !' means 'I am doing well, thank you!'.

questions.prompt: Put together: 'Very good, thank you, and you?'
questions.explanation: 'Très bien, merci, et vous ?' is a polite reply.

questions.prompt: When parting from someone in the afternoon, which wish is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: 'Bonne journée !' means 'Have a good day!'.

questions.prompt: Listen to the farewell phrase. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: 'Au revoir et à bientôt !' translates to 'Goodbye and see you soon!'.

questions.sentence: Passez une excellente ___ ! (Have a great evening!)
questions.explanation: 'Bonne soirée' or 'une excellente soirée' wishes a good evening.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between 'Tu' and 'Vous' in French?
options: 'Tu' is informal (friends, children, family); 'Vous' is polite/formal or plural
'Tu' is only for women; 'Vous' is for men
'Tu' is used in the morning; 'Vous' at night
They are completely interchangeable in all contexts
questions.correctAnswer: 'Tu' is informal (friends, children, family); 'Vous' is polite/formal or plural
questions.explanation: Using 'vous' with strangers, elders, and professionals shows essential respect (vouvoiement).

questions.prompt: Match the farewell expressions:

pairs.english: See you in a little while

questions.prompt: Listen to the phrase. In what context is 'Je vous en prie' used?

To order food in a restaurant
To ask what time it is
questions.correctAnswer: As a courteous formal response to 'Merci' (You're welcome)

questions.sentence: Pardon madame, ___ -moi de vous déranger.

questions.prompt: Assemble: 'S'il vous plaît, monsieur'

questions.prompt: What is the traditional French physical greeting among friends and relatives called?
questions.explanation: 'La bise' is the customary exchange of light kisses on the cheeks between close acquaintances.

questions.prompt: How is 'Comment vas-tu ?' used compared to 'Comment allez-vous ?'?
options: It is informal, addressed to a friend or child
It is formal, addressed to a boss
It is plural, addressed to a group
It is used only in emails

questions.explanation: 'Comment vas-tu ?' uses the informal pronoun 'tu'.

questions.prompt: Match the polite social titles:
When someone says 'Merci beaucoup', which of the following is NOT an appropriate reply?

questions.prompt: Match the introduction phrases:

questions.prompt: Assemble: 'Je m'appelle Marie et voici Paul'

questions.explanation: 'Je vous présente...' means 'I introduce to you / This is...'.

questions.prompt: Match identity terms with English:

questions.sentence: Je te ___ mon collègue Alexandre.
questions.explanation: 'Je te présente...' is used to introduce someone informally.

questions.prompt: How do you say 'He is called Pierre' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Il s'appelle...' is the third person singular masculine ('He is called...').

questions.prompt: Match subject pronouns with 's'appeler' conjugations:

options: Delighted to meet you! / Pleased to meet you!
questions.correctAnswer: Delighted to meet you! / Pleased to meet you!
questions.explanation: 'Ravi de vous rencontrer !' expresses delight in meeting someone.

questions.sentence: Elles ___ Sophie et Camille.
questions.explanation: Third person plural feminine takes 's'appellent'.

questions.prompt: Which answer correctly answers 'Qui est-ce ?' (Who is this?)?
questions.explanation: 'C'est mon ami Nicolas' (This is my friend Nicolas) directly identifies a person.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Nationalities, Countries & 'Être'
lessons.description: Master the verb 'Être' (to be), express country origins, and form masculine and feminine nationalities.

Only if they refer to food

questions.sentence: Le cours commence ___ neuf heures du matin.
questions.explanation: At a specific time takes the preposition 'à': 'à neuf heures'.

questions.prompt: Match parts of the day:
Assemble: 'À quelle heure ouvrez-vous ?'
questions.explanation: 'À quelle heure ouvrez-vous ?' asks 'What time do you open?'.

questions.prompt: Why does 'une heure' NOT have an 's' at the end, while 'deux heures' does?
options: Because 'une' is singular (1 hour); 'deux' is plural (hours)
Silent letters are optional in French
questions.correctAnswer: Because 'une' is singular (1 hour); 'deux' is plural (hours)
questions.explanation: 'Il est une heure' (singular); 'Il est deux heures' (plural with 's').

questions.prompt: Listen to the phrase. What does 'presque' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Presque' means almost / nearly.

questions.sentence: Il est trois heures moins ___ (2:50).

questions.prompt: How do you say 'It's time to go' in colloquial French?

questions.prompt: Match duration words with English:
When will the speaker arrive?
questions.phrase: Je serai là dans une demi-heure.
questions.explanation: 'Une demi-heure' means half an hour.

questions.prompt: Assemble: 'Il est minuit pile'
questions.explanation: 'Il est minuit pile' means 'It is midnight on the dot'.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Reflexive Verbs & Morning Routine
lessons.description: Describe daily routines using reflexive verbs (se lever, se laver, s'habiller) and adverbs of frequency.

questions.prompt: What marks a reflexive verb in French (e.g. 'se lever')?
options: The reflexive pronoun 'se' showing that the subject performs the action on themselves
An accent on the final vowel
It is only used in the past tense
questions.correctAnswer: The reflexive pronoun 'se' showing that the subject performs the action on themselves
questions.explanation: Reflexive verbs use pronouns matching the subject (me, te, se, nous, vous, se).

questions.prompt: Match reflexive pronouns with subject pronouns:
Listen to the sentence. What time does the speaker wake up?
questions.phrase: Je me réveille à sept heures.
questions.explanation: 'Se réveiller' means to wake up: 'Je me réveille à 7h'.

questions.sentence: Après le réveil, je me ___ du lit. (I get up)
questions.explanation: 'Se lever' means to get out of bed / get up: 'je me lève'.

questions.prompt: Match morning routine actions:
What is the difference between 'se réveiller' and 'se lever'?
options: 'Se réveiller' is waking up; 'Se lever' is physically getting out of bed
'Se réveiller' is getting dressed; 'Se lever' is taking a shower
They are exact synonyms with no difference
'Se lever' is only for the evening
questions.correctAnswer: 'Se réveiller' is waking up; 'Se lever' is physically getting out of bed
questions.explanation: You can wake up ('se réveiller') at 7:00 but stay in bed until you get up ('se lever') at 7:15.

questions.prompt: What routine step is this?
questions.explanation: 'Prendre le petit déjeuner' means to eat breakfast.

questions.prompt: Assemble: 'Elle se brosse les dents'
questions.explanation: 'Elle se brosse les dents' means 'She brushes her teeth'.

questions.sentence: Tu te ___ à quelle heure le matin ? (What time do you get up?)
questions.explanation: With 'tu', the ending is -es: 'Tu te lèves'.

questions.prompt: Match evening routine actions:
How do you say 'I go to bed at 11:00 PM'?
options: Je me couche à vingt-trois heures
Je me lève à onze heures
questions.correctAnswer: Je me couche à vingt-trois heures
questions.explanation: 'Se coucher' is the verb for going to bed: 'Je me couche à 23h'.

questions.prompt: Listen to the audio. What are they doing?
questions.explanation: 'Se préparer' means to get ready.

questions.prompt: Match frequency adverbs with English:

questions.sentence: Je ne me lève ___ avant huit heures le dimanche.
questions.explanation: Negative frequency: 'ne... jamais' means 'never' ('I never get up before 8:00').

questions.prompt: Assemble: 'D'habitude, je prends le métro'
questions.explanation: 'D'habitude, je prends le métro' means 'Usually, I take the subway'.

questions.prompt: How is negation formed with a reflexive verb in the present tense?
options: ne + reflexive pronoun + verb + pas (e.g. 'Je ne me lave pas')
questions.correctAnswer: ne + reflexive pronoun + verb + pas (e.g. 'Je ne me lave pas')
questions.explanation: 'Ne' comes before the reflexive pronoun, and 'pas' comes after the verb: 'Je ne me lève pas'.

questions.prompt: What does 's'endormir' mean?
questions.explanation: 'S'endormir' means to fall asleep.

questions.prompt: Match daily transport routine verbs:

questions.sentence: Vous vous ___ à quelle heure le soir ? (What time do you go to bed?)
questions.explanation: 'Se coucher' is the verb for going to bed: 'Vous vous couchez'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly says 'I hurry up'?
questions.explanation: 'Se dépêcher' is reflexive: 'Je me dépêche' (I am hurrying up).

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Weather, Seasons & Climate
lessons.description: Discuss weather forecasts with 'faire', describe rain and snow, and talk about the four seasons.

questions.prompt: Which verb is used for most weather expressions in French (e.g. 'It is sunny / cold')?
options: Faire (Il fait beau, Il fait froid)
questions.correctAnswer: Faire (Il fait beau, Il fait froid)
questions.explanation: French uses the impersonal 'Il fait + adjective/noun': 'Il fait beau', 'Il fait chaud'.

questions.prompt: Match French weather phrases with English:
Listen to the audio. What is happening outside?
questions.explanation: 'Il pleut' comes from the verb 'pleuvoir' (to rain).

questions.sentence: En hiver dans les Alpes, il ___ beaucoup. (It snows)
questions.explanation: 'Il neige' means 'It snows / It is snowing'.

questions.prompt: Match the four seasons in French:
Which season uses the preposition 'au' instead of 'en'?
options: Au printemps (Spring - begins with a consonant)
questions.correctAnswer: Au printemps (Spring - begins with a consonant)
questions.explanation: 'Au printemps' takes 'au', while summer, autumn, and winter take 'en' (en été, en automne, en hiver) because they begin with vowels!

questions.prompt: What does this common question mean?
questions.explanation: 'Quel temps fait-il ?' asks 'What's the weather like?'.

questions.prompt: Assemble: 'Il fait du soleil et du vent'
questions.explanation: 'Il fait du soleil et du vent' means 'It is sunny and windy'.

questions.prompt: Match sky conditions with English:

pairs.english: There are clouds / It is cloudy

questions.sentence: Prends ton parapluie, il y a de l'___ dehors. (storm)
questions.explanation: 'Un orage' is a thunderstorm.

questions.prompt: How do you say 'The temperature is 20 degrees'?
questions.explanation: 'Il fait vingt degrés' (Celsius) expresses temperature.

questions.prompt: Listen to the statement. What is the condition?
questions.explanation: 'Geler' means to freeze: 'Il gèle' = it is freezing.

questions.prompt: Match weather items with English:
Assemble: 'En été, il fait très chaud'
questions.explanation: 'En été, il fait très chaud' means 'In summer, it is very hot'.

questions.sentence: Les feuilles tombent en ___ (Autumn).
questions.explanation: 'En automne' means in autumn.

questions.prompt: What does 'un temps de chien' mean idiomatically in French?
questions.explanation: 'Un temps de chien' is a colorful idiom for dreadful, rainy weather.

questions.prompt: Listen to the weather report. What is occurring on the coast?
questions.phrase: Il y a beaucoup de vent sur la côte.
questions.explanation: 'Beaucoup de vent' means a lot of wind.

questions.prompt: Match climate terms:

questions.sentence: Regarde le bulletin ___ à la télévision.
questions.explanation: 'Le bulletin météo' is the weather forecast report.

questions.prompt: When the sky is completely grey and covered with clouds, the French say:
questions.explanation: 'Le ciel est couvert' means the sky is overcast.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Café Culture & Ordering
lessons.description: Experience Parisian café culture: order drinks, pastries, specify indoor or terrace seating, and request the bill politely.

questions.prompt: How do you politely order a coffee with milk and a croissant in a French café?
options: Un café au lait et un croissant, s'il vous plaît
Je veux café et croissant immédiatement
Donne-moi un café et un pain
Prenez un café avec du pain
questions.correctAnswer: Un café au lait et un croissant, s'il vous plaît
questions.explanation: 'Un café au lait et un croissant, s'il vous plaît' is polite, natural, and standard.

questions.prompt: Match French café beverages with their English translations:
Listen to the customer speaking to the server. What are they asking for?
questions.explanation: 'L'addition, s'il vous plaît' means 'The bill, please'.

questions.sentence: Bonjour, je ___ un thé à la menthe, s'il vous plaît.
questions.explanation: 'Je voudrais' (I would like) is the classic polite formula for ordering in French.

questions.prompt: Assemble the polite request: 'Pour moi, un verre d'eau'
questions.explanation: 'Pour moi, un verre d'eau' means 'For me, a glass of water'.

questions.prompt: If you want free tap water at a French café, what specific phrase do you use?
options: Une carafe d'eau, s'il vous plaît
questions.correctAnswer: Une carafe d'eau, s'il vous plaît
questions.explanation: In France, 'une carafe d'eau' is a pitcher of tap water provided free of charge by law with meals/orders.

questions.prompt: Match French café seating & service terms:
Listen to the customer entering the restaurant. What seating do they request?
questions.phrase: Deux personnes en terrasse, s'il vous plaît.
options: Table for two outside on the terrace
Table for two indoors near the window
Table for four in the back
questions.correctAnswer: Table for two outside on the terrace
questions.explanation: 'En terrasse' means on the outdoor terrace.

questions.prompt: What is 'un pain au chocolat' also called in Southwestern France?
questions.explanation: In Southwestern France, a pain au chocolat is famously called 'une chocolatine'.

questions.sentence: Est-ce que le service est ___ dans l'addition ?
questions.explanation: 'Service compris' means the service tip is already included in the bill in France.

questions.prompt: Match popular breakfast bakery items in France:

pairs.english: Slice of baguette with butter and jam

questions.prompt: Listen to the waiter's question. What are they asking you?
questions.explanation: 'Vous désirez autre chose ?' means 'Would you like anything else?'.

questions.prompt: Assemble: 'Ce sera tout, merci beaucoup'
questions.explanation: 'Ce sera tout, merci beaucoup' means 'That will be all, thank you very much'.

questions.prompt: How do you ask for still water versus sparkling water?
options: De l'eau plate vs de l'eau gazeuse / pétillante
De l'eau douce vs de l'eau dure
De l'eau blanche vs de l'eau noire
De l'eau chaude vs de l'eau tiède
questions.correctAnswer: De l'eau plate vs de l'eau gazeuse / pétillante
questions.explanation: 'Eau plate' is still (non-carbonated) water, while 'eau gazeuse' or 'pétillante' is sparkling.

questions.sentence: Garçon ! Une ___ d'eau fraîche, s'il vous plaît.
questions.explanation: 'Une carafe d'eau' is a jug or carafe of water.

questions.prompt: What does this restaurant inquiry ask?
questions.phrase: Quel est le plat du jour aujourd'hui ?
questions.explanation: 'Le plat du jour' is the dish of the day / daily special in French bistros.

questions.prompt: Match French restaurant courses with English equivalents:
How do French people say 'Enjoy your meal!' before eating?
questions.explanation: 'Bon appétit !' means 'Enjoy your meal!'.

questions.sentence: Je prends le menu à midi : entrée, plat et ___.
questions.explanation: A standard French set menu includes entrée, plat, and dessert.

questions.prompt: Assemble: 'Une table pour deux personnes, s'il vous plaît'
questions.explanation: 'Une table pour deux personnes, s'il vous plaît' = 'A table for two, please'.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Groceries & Partitive Articles
lessons.description: Shop at the bakery, butcher, market, and supermarket using partitive articles (du, de la, de l', des) and expressions of quantity.

questions.prompt: Which partitive article is used before a masculine singular uncountable food like 'pain' (bread)?
questions.explanation: 'Du' (de + le) is used with masculine singular nouns: 'du pain' (some bread), 'du fromage' (some cheese).

questions.prompt: Match French partitive articles with correct food combinations:

pairs.native: de la viande / de la confiture

pairs.english: some water / oil (starts with vowel / silent h)

questions.prompt: Listen to the grocery shopper. What two items are they purchasing?
questions.phrase: Je voudrais un kilo de tomates et deux baguettes, s'il vous plaît.
options: 3 cucumbers and a loaf of sourdough
questions.explanation: 'Un kilo de tomates et deux baguettes' = '1 kilo of tomatoes and 2 baguettes'.

questions.prompt: In a negative sentence, what do partitive articles (du, de la, des) turn into?
options: de / d' (Je ne mange pas de viande)
le / la (Je ne mange le viande)
un / une (Je ne mange une viande)
questions.correctAnswer: de / d' (Je ne mange pas de viande)
questions.explanation: In negative sentences, partitive articles become 'de' (or 'd'' before a vowel): 'Je ne mange pas de viande'.

questions.sentence: Elle ne boit pas ___ café le soir.
questions.explanation: After negation 'ne ... pas', 'du café' becomes 'de café'.

questions.prompt: Match French food shops with what you buy there:
Listen to the customer at the bakery. How do they like their baguette?
questions.phrase: À la boulangerie, j'achète une baguette tradition bien cuite.
questions.explanation: 'Bien cuite' means well-baked and crusty in French bakery lingo.

questions.prompt: Assemble: 'Combien coûte un kilo de pommes ?'
questions.explanation: 'Combien coûte un kilo de pommes ?' means 'How much does a kilo of apples cost?'.

questions.prompt: Match French quantity containers with English:

pairs.english: A packet / box of (e.g. pasta, biscuits)

questions.sentence: Donnez-moi trois ___ de jambon blanc, s'il vous plaît.
questions.explanation: 'Tranches' means slices (slices of ham).

questions.prompt: Which expression means 'a lot of' and always takes 'de'?
questions.explanation: Quantity adverbs like 'beaucoup de' (a lot of), 'un peu de' (a little), and 'trop de' (too much) all take invariable 'de'.

questions.prompt: Listen to the shopping list. What quantity of strawberries does the speaker need?
questions.phrase: Il me faut un litre de lait et cinq cents grammes de fraises.
questions.explanation: 'Cinq cents grammes de fraises' = 500 grams of strawberries.

questions.prompt: Assemble: 'Je mange du pain avec du beurre'
questions.explanation: 'Je mange du pain avec du beurre' means 'I eat bread with butter'.

questions.sentence: Au petit déjeuner, il boit ___ jus d'orange.
questions.explanation: 'Jus' is masculine singular, so 'du jus d'orange' (some orange juice) is required.

questions.prompt: Match French vegetables with English:
How do you ask a merchant 'Is that everything?' in French?
questions.explanation: Shopkeepers in France famously ask 'Et avec ceci ?' meaning 'And with this? / Anything else?'.

questions.prompt: What does the market vendor say about the strawberries?
questions.phrase: Les fraises sont très fraîches et de saison.
options: They are very fresh and in season
They were imported from far away
questions.correctAnswer: They are very fresh and in season
questions.explanation: 'Très fraîches et de saison' means very fresh and in season.

questions.sentence: Il achète une douzaine ___ œufs au marché.
questions.explanation: 'Une douzaine d'œufs' (a dozen eggs): before a vowel, 'de' elides to 'd''.

questions.prompt: Match French dairy and pantry items:
Assemble: 'Il n'y a plus de fromage dans le réfrigérateur'
questions.explanation: 'Il n'y a plus de fromage dans le réfrigérateur' means 'There is no more cheese in the fridge'.

questions.explanation: 'Gardez la monnaie' tells the taxi driver or waiter to keep the change as a tip.

questions.sentence: Vous désirez votre ___ de caisse ?

A swimming pool and a tennis court
A balcony facing the main street

Ma cuisine est petite et froide
Mon lit est propre et doux

questions.sentence: Continuez jusqu'au feu ___ (traffic light).

Across the river on the left

questions.explanation: 'Au coin de la rue, à côté de la boulangerie' = At the corner of the street, next to the bakery.

C'est très loin, à trois heures de vol

Change trains at the central station
Stay on the train until the terminus
